Feature: USB xHCI Host Controller High-Speed Device Enumeration
Test Description: Initialize the USB xHCI host controller, configure the USB2 PHY, read capability registers (HCSPARAMS1, HCSPARAMS2, PAGESIZE, SUPTPRT2_DW2, SUPTPRT3_DW2), configure operational registers (CONFIG, DCBAAP, CRCR), set up the Event Ring Segment Table and Event Ring, enable interrupts, run the controller, perform a port reset on PORTSC_20, enable wake-on-connect/disconnect/overcurrent, call set_address to issue Enable Slot and Address Device commands, configure the Input Context (Slot Context and Endpoint 0 Context), ring the doorbell, and call enumeration to issue GET_DESCRIPTOR requests for Device and Qualifier descriptors. Verify port connect status and event completions. Finish with pass status.
Remarks: The Default_IRQHandler uses logical AND (&&) instead of bitwise AND (&) for checking bit 31 of MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, which is a potential bug - it evaluates true for any non-zero value. Three system register macros (MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_MSK_STS0, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) are unresolved as lss_sysreg headers are not in the available corpus. RAM-based memory macros (Device_Context_Base_Address_Array, Device_Context_Array, Default_Event_Ring_Array, Default_Command_Ring, Default_Input_Context, Event_Ring_Segment_Table) have ambiguous base addresses due to conditional RAM definition in headers. GIC_EnableIRQ(84) is commented out in favor of GIC_EnableAllIRQ().
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Call nic_programming() to initialize NIC subsystem.
2. Call GIC_EnableAllIRQ() to enable all GIC interrupts.
3. Read and write PHY Control Register at MIZAR_USB_BASE+0xC200 with value 0x102407.
4. Read HCSPARAMS1 to obtain port_count.
5. Read SUPTPRT2_DW2 and SUPTPRT3_DW2 for supported protocol information.
6. Read PORTSC_20 for initial port status.
7. Read HCSPARAMS2 and PAGESIZE for controller capabilities.
8. Write CONFIG register with 0x10 (MaxSlotsEn), then read back and write 0x110 (CIE enabled).
Impacted Registers: HCSPARAMS1 (offset 0x4, read for port_count), HCSPARAMS2 (offset 0x8, read for capabilities), PAGESIZE (offset 0x28, read), SUPTPRT2_DW2 (offset 0x898, read), SUPTPRT3_DW2 (offset 0x8A8, read), CONFIG (offset 0x58, write 0x10 then 0x110), DCBAAP_LO (offset 0x50, write), DCBAAP_HI (offset 0x54, write 0x0), CRCR_LO (offset 0x38, write Default_Command_Ring+0x1), CRCR_HI (offset 0x3C, write 0x0), ERSTSZ (offset 0x468, write 0x1), ERDP_LO (offset 0x478, write/advance through offsets 0x18/0x28/0x38/0x48/0x58/0x68), ERDP_HI (offset 0x47C, write 0x0), ERSTBA_LO (offset 0x470, write Event_Ring_Segment_Table), ERSTBA_HI (offset 0x474, write 0x0), IMOD (offset 0x464, write 0x0), IMAN (offset 0x460, write 0x2 and 0x1), USBCMD (offset 0x20, write 0x4 and 0x5), USBSTS (offset 0x24, read and write 0x8), PORTSC_20 (offset 0x420, read and write 0xe0006f1/0xe220200/0xe200e01/0xe0002a0), DBOFF (offset 0x14, read for db_offset)
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. After running the controller (USBCMD=0x5), the interrupt must fire and PORTSC_20 port connect status (CCS) should be high.
2. USBSTS Event Interrupt (EINT) bit must be clearable by writing 0x8.
3. Enable Slot Command must complete successfully (event completion read from Event Ring).
4. Address Device Command must complete successfully (event completion read from Event Ring).
5. GET_DESCRIPTOR (Device) and GET_DESCRIPTOR (Qualifier) transfers must complete via event ring completion events.
6. Interrupt handler must correctly identify USB interrupt source from MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0 bit 31, acknowledge via IMAN and clear via GIC_ClearIRQ(84).
7. Port reset via PORTSC_20=0xe0006f1 must complete and port status must reflect connected high-speed device.
8. Test completes with finish(0) indicating pass.

Feature: USB DWC3 Device Controller Full-Speed Bulk Transfer
Test Description: Configure the USB DWC3 device controller in device mode for full-speed operation. Initialize the event buffer (GEVNTADRLO/HI/SIZ/COUNT), configure global control (GCTL) for device mode, set device configuration (DCFG), enable device events (DEVTEN), configure user control (GUCTL), issue DEPSTARTCFG command via set_configuration, configure transfer resources for 8 endpoints using DEPXFERCFG loop, enable physical endpoints 0 and 1 (DALEPENA), set device control (DCTL), enable system-level interrupt (INTR_EN0). Perform USB enumeration: handle setup/status stages, process SET_CONFIGURATION and GET_DESCRIPTOR (Configuration) requests with 60-byte configuration descriptor containing 6 endpoint descriptors (bulk and interrupt). Configure USB2 PHY (GUSB2PHYCFG). Set device address via DCFG. Execute bulk data transfer on EP4 with 64-byte max packet size using Buffer_PointerLO_1 and StartXfer command (0x506). Verify transfer completion via interrupt-driven event processing.
Remarks: The Default_IRQHandler uses logical AND (&&) instead of bitwise AND (&) for checking bit 31 of MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, which is a potential bug - it evaluates true for any non-zero value. Four system/device register macros are unresolved: MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_MSK_STS0, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0 (lss_sysreg headers not in corpus), MIZAR_USB_DCFG (macro definition not found in header corpus though USB_DCFG_OFFSET=0xC700 exists). Seven register macros have ambiguous offsets due to dual definitions in headers: MIZAR_USB_GEVNTADRLO, MIZAR_USB_GEVNTADRHI, MIZAR_USB_GEVNTSIZ, MIZAR_USB_GEVNTCOUNT, MIZAR_USB_DEPCMDPAR1, MIZAR_USB_DEPCMDPAR0, MIZAR_USB_DEPCMD. RAM-based memory macros (Default_Event_Ring_Array, Buffer_PointerLO, Buffer_PointerLO_1, event_trb_addr) have ambiguous base addresses due to conditional RAM definition in headers. MIZAR_USB_GUSB2PHYCFG is used in source but was not in the original 22-macro list from Agent 2. The variable event_comletion appears to be a typo for event_completion. Debug markers 0xdeadbee4 and 0xdeadbee5 are written to address 0xA0243ffc to track enumeration progress. The DCFG register is written twice: first with 0x480801 during init, then with 0x480809 during SET ADDRESS.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Call nic_programming() to initialize NIC subsystem.
2. Call GIC_EnableAllIRQ() to enable all GIC interrupts.
3. Clear 20 DWORD entries at Buffer_PointerLO and event_trb_addr to zero.
4. Configure event buffer: write GEVNTADRLO=Default_Event_Ring_Array, GEVNTADRHI=0x0, GEVNTSIZ=0x30 (48 bytes), GEVNTCOUNT=0x0.
5. Read GCTL, then write GCTL=0x30c12214 to set device mode port direction.
6. Read DCFG, then write DCFG=0x480801 for device configuration.
7. Write DEVTEN=0x1f to enable device events (USB reset, connect done, disconnect, etc.).
8. Read GUCTL, then write GUCTL=0xa400010 for user control settings.
Impacted Registers: GCTL (offset 0xC110, read then write 0x30c12214 for device mode), DCTL (offset 0xC704, write 0x80f00000 to start device controller), DALEPENA (offset 0xC720, write 0x3 to enable physical EP 0 and 1), DEVTEN (offset 0xC708, write 0x1f to enable device events), GUCTL (offset 0xC12C, read then write 0xa400010), DSTS (offset 0xC70C, read in Default_IRQHandler for status)
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. All 8 endpoint DEPXFERCFG commands (0x402) must complete successfully (DEPCMD register value changes from 0x402 for each endpoint).
2. All StartXfer commands (0x506) on EP0, EP1, and EP4 must complete successfully (DEPCMD register value changes from 0x506).
3. DEPSTARTCFG command (0x409) issued via set_configuration must complete.
4. Interrupt handler must correctly read GEVNTCOUNT, store to event_counter, and write back to acknowledge events.
5. Interrupt handler must identify USB interrupt source from MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0 bit 31 and clear via GIC_ClearIRQ(84).
6. Configuration descriptor (60 bytes) must be correctly written to Buffer_PointerLO with valid USB descriptor format.
7. SET ADDRESS must succeed by writing DCFG=0x480809.
8. Bulk transfer on EP4 with 64-byte payload using Buffer_PointerLO_1 must complete via interrupt-driven event processing.
9. USB2 PHY must be configured with GUSB2PHYCFG=0x40002547.
10. All interrupt-driven wait loops (int_pend) must be serviced by Default_IRQHandler.
